name: On the ISS
description: Low Earth orbit. Your medical team answers almost in real time. Spica guides, records and sends.
source: S06; S37 (731 µSv/day in 2019, via S47); S15
comm_policy: Near real time, but Maia queues the report for the next downlink; nothing waits for a reply.

name: Spacewalk (EVA)
comm_delay_label: Voice loop with crew inside + Mission Control
description: Outside the station in the suit. Few numbers, large icons, hands-free. Extra EVA dose: mean 26 µGy/h in the suit; a worst-case EVA ≈ 7 days on the ISS.
evidence_level: estimate (EVA dose is absorbed dose, mGy); demo (stricter rules)
comm_policy: Voice loop; Maia shows suit data hands-free and logs the EVA as an event.

name: Back on Earth
description: Readapting to gravity: dizziness, low blood pressure when standing up, falls. A new baseline starts 7 days after landing.
comm_policy: Connected; same analysis, new baseline after landing.

name: Lunar Surface
description: Preview. No magnetic field to shield you; frequent spacewalks; lunar dust.
comm_policy: Seconds of delay; act first, report with the next downlink.

name: Mars Transit
comm_delay_label: Messages arrive in X min – sent when possible
description: Preview. One-way delay ~3–22 min (cap 23). About every 26 months the Sun blocks the link for 13–21 days. The crew medical officer acts first.
comm_policy: Minutes of delay and 13–21-day blackouts: offline-first, store-and-forward.
